title: Application of n-of-1 treatment trials in schizophrenia: systematic review

cost.compute_notes: JATS full text from Europe PMC rendered with tools/jats2txt.py to 32,985 characters. Table 1 transcribed by hand into artifacts/marwick2018_table1.csv with four derived columns the paper does not have (replicate_cycles, is_antipsychotic_vs_placebo, raw_data_reported, n_patients per study). No simulation, no reanalysis: the counting is arithmetic on their own table, which is why the depth is read-full-text and not read-and-reanalysed.

triggers: how many n-of-1 trials exist in schizophrenia
has anyone measured individual response to antipsychotics directly
is there empirical evidence for individual treatment response in psychosis
what evidence supports personalising antipsychotic treatment
the design that identifies patient-by-treatment interaction, has it been run

claims.statement: Six n-of-1 trials in schizophrenia exist in the published literature to January 2017, with wide methodological variability and all at high risk of bias.
claims.scope: 4,727 citations screened across the major electronic databases; English-language peer-reviewed studies meeting the CENT 2015 definition of an n-of-1 trial in a patient with schizophrenia.

quantities.name: n_of_1_studies_found
quantities.source: Marwick et al. 2018, Results and Fig. 1. 4,727 citations were screened to find them; that is a screening volume, not a denominator -- 6/4727 is not a rate of anything, so count/denominator are deliberately absent.

quantities.name: total_patients_across_all_n_of_1_trials
quantities.source: maria 2026, derived from their Table 1: five single-patient studies plus one series of four

our_assessment.why: A systematic review with a stated search, a screening protocol and a PRISMA flow. I have not repeated the search, so this is accepted at the depth read: their inventory, not my verification of its completeness. The count that matters is not theirs but the arithmetic on their Table 1, in c2.

claims.statement: Not one of these trials compared an antipsychotic against placebo, only two used a design with replicated cycles, and none reported comprehensive raw data. The empirical basis for individual response to antipsychotic medication, from designs capable of identifying it, is two patients — neither of whom was taking the drug in question.
claims.scope: Arithmetic on their Table 1, which I transcribed. 'Replicated cycles' means at least two independent A-vs-B comparisons in the same patient, which is Senn's requirement for identifying patient-by-treatment interaction.

quantities.name: trials_comparing_an_antipsychotic_against_placebo
quantities.source: maria 2026, artifacts/marwick2018_table1.csv. The interventions were: add-on L-dopa, add-on donepezil, a right ear plug, transcranial magnetic stimulation, exercise counselling, and a cognitive intervention.

quantities.name: studies_with_two_or_more_replicate_cycles
quantities.source: maria 2026: two ABAB designs (Alford 1986, MacEwan 2001). The other four are ABA, BAB or ABAC, each giving one comparison per patient.

quantities.name: patients_in_designs_that_identify_the_interaction
quantities.source: maria 2026: one patient in each of the two ABAB studies

quantities.name: studies_reporting_comprehensive_raw_data
quantities.source: maria 2026, from their own narrative: three offered graphs and tables 'but did not report comprehensive raw data scores', three employed statistical tests 'but lacked both full reporting of the tests and the raw data used', one 'gave a selective sample of raw data only'

quantities.name: studies_with_any_blinding
quantities.source: maria 2026: one double-blind, one blinding secondary assessors only

our_assessment.why: This is the empirical closure of the whole area and it is arithmetic, not interpretation. senn2016-mastering-variation#c1 establishes that only replication within patients identifies patient-by-treatment interaction. Marwick et al. inventory every study in schizophrenia that even attempts that design. The intersection of 'replicated cycles' and 'antipsychotic versus placebo' is EMPTY. So the question that 66 trials and 17,202 patients have been argued about — does response to antipsychotics differ between individuals — has never once been addressed by a design that could answer it, in any patient. Two patients have been studied in a design of the right shape, on donepezil and on a cognitive intervention, without raw data. THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS: their search ends January 2017, so eight years of possible trials are outside it, and I have not searched forward. Do not quote this as the present-day count; quote it as the count to 2017 and say so.

claims.statement: The zero still holds in 2026. A forward search from January 2017 finds no n-of-1 or repeated-crossover trial of an antipsychotic against placebo in schizophrenia.
claims.scope: My search, not theirs. Europe PMC, title-restricted, 2017-01-01 to 2026-12-31.

quantities.name: new_nof1_psychosis_titles_since_2017
quantities.source: maria 2026: Europe PMC TITLE:"n-of-1" AND (TITLE:schizophrenia OR TITLE:antipsychotic OR TITLE:psychosis) returns 7 hits ever; 3 are post-2017 and none is an antipsychotic-vs-placebo trial

quantities.name: new_antipsychotic_vs_placebo_nof1_trials_since_2017
quantities.source: maria 2026: eszopiclone for negative symptoms (a hypnotic, and self-described as an UNINTENDED n-of-1); five systemic n-of-1 trials of MUSIC THERAPY; and one HYPOTHETICAL case of using n-of-1 for ADHD in psychosis

our_assessment.why: The caveat attached to c2 -- that the review's search ended January 2017 -- is now closed, and the answer did not change. Nine years on, the design that identifies individual response to antipsychotics has still never been pointed at antipsychotics. LIMITS OF MY SEARCH, stated so nobody over-reads it: title-restricted and English-language, on one index. A trial reported without 'n-of-1' in its title -- described instead as a 'repeated crossover' or 'single-case experimental design' -- would be missed, and SCED is a live term in psychology. The honest claim is 'nothing under this name', which is weaker than 'nothing'.

checked.result: USABLE. Table 1 renders as cells, which is the whole content here. Note a duplicate deposit: PMC6429250 is the same article under a second PMCID (an erratum or a second deposit), and a naive search returns both as if they were two studies.

artifacts.locator: Marwick et al. 2018, Table 1, 'Study characteristics with key patient data'

checked.how: transcribed by hand from the rendered table; four columns added that the paper does not have (n_patients, replicate_cycles, is_antipsychotic_vs_placebo, raw_data_reported), each derived from the paper's own design and narrative text
checked.result: 6 rows. My coding of replicate_cycles is the one judgement call: ABAB and ABAB score 2 because each contains two independent A-vs-B comparisons in the same patient; ABA, BAB and ABAC score 1. ABAC is arguably 0 for the A-vs-B question since C is a different comparator. Coding it 0 would not change any claim.

datasheet.composition: One row per included study: patient characteristics, design, duration, intervention, comparator, blinding, outcome measures, analysis, result, plus the four derived columns.
datasheet.caveats: Duration for Alford 1986 is not reported in the source and is null here. Durations given in weeks were converted from months where the paper used months (Done 1986: 5 months -> 21.7 weeks); the conversion is mine and is approximate.

artifacts.fetch_cmd: curl -s -G https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search --data-urlencode 'query=TITLE:"n-of-1" AND (TITLE:schizophrenia OR TITLE:antipsychotic OR TITLE:psychosis)' --data-urlencode format=json

checked.how: ran the command above and a second variant restricted by FIRST_PDATE with abstract terms
checked.result: 7 hits in total for the title query, of which 2 are the Marwick review itself under its two PMCIDs, 2 are unrelated medicinal-chemistry papers whose compound names begin with N-, and 3 are genuine post-2017 n-of-1 work in psychosis: eszopiclone, music therapy, and a hypothetical ADHD case. None is an antipsychotic against placebo.

relations.why: Senn establishes that only replication within patients identifies the interaction. This inventories how often that has been done in schizophrenia: six times, two of them with replicated cycles, nine patients in total.

Their conclusion that a quarter of patients gain more than 17 PANSS points calls for personalisation. The design that could test that claim has been used on zero patients taking an antipsychotic against placebo.

Their conclusion -- assume the average effect applies to the individual -- is the safer of the two positions given the evidence, but it is equally unsupported by any design that identifies the individual effect. The honest statement is that nobody knows.

open_questions: My forward search was title-restricted. A repeated-crossover trial described as a 'single-case experimental design' (SCED) rather than an n-of-1 would be missed, and SCED is the live term in psychology rather than psychiatry. Searching SCED plus antipsychotic is the remaining gap and is one query.

The same inventory for DEPRESSION would matter more for my own corpus, since the antidepressant data are the ones I can reach. If replicated-crossover antidepressant trials exist with raw data, sigma_C is directly estimable there and the whole aggregate dispute has an empirical anchor.

Statins have an n-of-1 trial SERIES with modern methodology (StatinWISE and the series Marwick cites for muscle pain). That is outside psychiatry but it is a worked example of the design at scale, and it would show what sigma_C looks like when someone actually measures it.
